plants.name: Hyacinthoides non-scripta
plants.description: Woodland floors across Britain turn into shimmering lakes of violet-blue as nodding, bell-shaped flowers hang from one side of arching stems. The blooms give off a sweet, delicate scent. Beech and oak woods are especially dramatic when the new leaves glow green overhead.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-April to late May, usually peaking in the first half of May
plants.location: Ancient woodlands of the United Kingdom and western Europe
plants.funFact: Britain holds about half of the world's bluebells. Because they grow so slowly from seed, they are protected by law, and bluebell woods are often treated as a sign of ancient woodland.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Cup-shaped flowers in nearly every color stand on sturdy stems. They line borders and fill whole fields in neat, bright stripes. Their glossy petals open wide in sunshine and close again at dusk.
plants.bloomingSeason: April to early May in cool temperate zones of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Gardens and bulb fields in the Netherlands and across northern Europe and North America
plants.funFact: In the 1630s, tulip bulbs sold in the Dutch Republic for prices that rivaled a grand canal house. The episode is remembered as 'tulip mania,' one of the earliest recorded speculative bubbles.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: Bare branches burst into clusters of magenta-pink, pea-like flowers. The blooms sprout straight from twigs and even the trunk before the heart-shaped leaves unfurl. In spring the tree looks like a cloud of rosy-purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to early May, later at cooler and more northern sites
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from the Great Lakes region to the southern United States
plants.funFact: Redbud flowers are edible and have a mild, tangy taste. Cooks sometimes add them to salads. The trunk-flowering habit is called cauliflory.
